label: Registry companion 1.0.0, proposed: hand-written synthetic vectors, staged in no corpus

vectors.description: A valid registry: two kinds, a reference cycle, an entry limited to one environment, a reference with a pointer, and a production overlay on a scalar, a secret and an array element.
The development environment's resolved document: no overlay applies, and every entry that applies in it is listed.
The production environment's resolved document: the overlay's pointers are replaced, and the entry limited to development is omitted.
An entry that fails step 5 is not checked by steps 6 and 7, and an entry whose production patch fails step 6 is checked by step 7 in development only.

Each entry-reference code, per environment: a target absent in one environment, a missing target, a malformed reference, a pointer that addresses nothing, a pointer that addresses a value only an overlay sets, and a kind the position does not allow. A cycle and a pointer that addresses a value are valid.
The secret-reference precedence: form, store and pin, a scope miss and a shared project, with a reference at its length bounds that is valid.

Step 2: excluded keywords, a back-reference, an array form of items, 17 and 16 branches, a recursive definition, an unknown member, an unreachable, a malformed and a repeated pointer pattern, and a secret pattern that is also a reference pattern. Entries of an invalid kind are not checked.

Pattern size counted as written: 4 096 is admitted and 4 097 is REG-KIND-PATTERN-LIMIT; (ab|ac){1000} is 5 000 as written, so it is refused even where an engine factors it smaller; a nested product of 1 002 is REG-KIND-PATTERN although {0} stops the chain above it, and a product of 1 000 under {0} is admitted. The reference runtime v0.47.0 admits (ab|ac){1000} (§17).

Step 4: a repeated kind name, a pin whose digest names a declaration of another version, a pin no supplied declaration matches, a deprecated kind and an unpinned declaration; and an entry of a kind the registry does not pin.
Each overlay code. A key that is not a pointer, or that no overlayable pattern matches, is located at its set member.
Step 8: more entries than maxEntries, and a resolved value one byte past maxEntryBytes beside one at it; the warnings for a deprecated member and for a secret reference in a registry without scopes.
A registry-level member error stops validation after step 3: the report names no registry digest, and nothing in the entries is checked.
A malformed entry is dropped and an order error is reported, and validation goes on to step 7 for the entries that remain.

Step 1: an integer one past 2^53 - 1 beside one at it, negative zero, and a decimal that does not round-trip beside one that does; a duplicate member and a later selector in two kind declarations. Step 2 still runs on the declarations step 1 admitted.
The batch for one kind in development: a decimal in normal form, a secret mapped to its store and scope, and references keyed by the referring pointer, one with a pointer into its target.
The same kind's batch in production, from overlaid values.
The registry the contract rows read is valid: a secret position that differs by environment is overlaid, and each environment's secret comes from its own project.
A closed kind's contract: required and optional members, an enumeration, an integer as a decimal, an array of strings, a secret, and a literal reference pattern whose target is closed.
A kind with open positions: each is listed once per type, and again once per type one token below, and nothing deeper.

Each advisory against the closed contract, and conditions that draw none, in applicability, an exception and rules, through all and not. Informative: the pack check is outside every conformance class of this version, and this row binds no claim.

Against the open contract: a pointer below an open position is listed, and a member the kind does not declare is not. Informative: the pack check is outside every conformance class of this version, and this row binds no claim.
Owns globs whose first segment holds a *: **, **/*, */**, * and gen*/x are each refused at their pointer, and gen/** and docs/*.md are not.

Owns globs held to the path rules: a colon, a device name with an extension, LPT and a superscript two, a segment ending in a dot or a space, .git, the short name GiT~1 and .git with a zero width joiner are refused; lpt0 and .github are not.

Response paths against gen/** and a/**/b: a/b and a/c/b are owned and gen is not; .git with a zero width non-joiner, GIT~1, a colon, aux.txt, COM and a superscript one, and segments ending in a space or a dot are refused; .gitkeep, com0 and ok.txt are not.
A response without diagnostics is refused at /diagnostics, though it holds no file and nothing to report.
Emitter warning codes: x-queue-unused and a code of 64 bytes are read; an upper-case letter or underscore, 65 bytes, an empty word, a trailing hyphen, x- alone and X- are refused at their code.
The request for a registry of one kind the manifest reads, in every environment: its declaration, its pin, both entries with their references as written, and the registry's digest.

The same registry with a pin, a declaration and an entry of a kind the manifest does not read: the request holds none of them, and differs from request-reads only in the registry's digest, which the harness's kind-filtering check restores (§11.5).

Two whole references of one project in one file pass, though they share a prefix of more than 32 characters; a reference cut before its version, one without its store, and one rewritten around its name and version fail, each for every reference it holds a run of.
The marker expected/~empty, a zero-byte regular file alone at the root of expected/, is read as no files.
A marker that is not zero bytes refuses the run.
A marker beside another file of expected/ refuses the run.
A marker below the root of expected/ refuses the run.
A vector with neither expected/ nor expected-failure.json refuses the run: a missing expected/ is never read as empty.
